summary: User asked about interaction between independent reviewer queue and new challenge-related Blocked dependencies. Reviewed Jarvis docs/specs/orchestration-architecture.md and current ReviewWorkflow.fs source: review requests are independently claimed from reviewer queue, immutable frozen source context, recorded as Unclaimed/Claimed/Accepted/ChangesRequested/Withdrawn, and Accepted/ChangesRequested decisions appear for original owner in agent_inbox UnacknowledgedFeedback; task owner phase/assignment unaffected by verdict. Reviewed feature/durable-agent-challenges docs: explicit block_on_challenges references challenge IDs, requeues dependent blocked attempts only when ALL challenge dependencies Satisfied, no auto Working or session launch, does not currently accept review IDs. Architectural recommendation: keep explicit independent reviewer queue/claim/verdict, do not reify every review as a Challenge or duplicate status. If optional review-wait is desired, reuse generic Blocked wait engine with typed Review(requestId) and Challenge(challengeId) prerequisites, but preserve first-class reviews. Review terminal verdict Accepted or ChangesRequested must unblock waiter to Ready to inspect feedback; Withdrawn should also wake with its outcome rather than strand, while claim does not wake. Blocking on review is optional; no automatic task completion/merge/approval from review, review must remain frozen. No source changes, task edits, assignments or deployment.
nextAction: On continuation, start agent_inbox. If operator wants implementation, check for existing task to extend blocked dependency mechanism with explicit review-id waits (separate from challenge ID and reviewer queue), ensure Accepted/ChangesRequested and Withdrawn terminal review outcomes produce durable Ready requeue or eligible deferred wakeup safely; reviewer claim must not wake. Maintain review's independent claim/decision and frozen source snapshots and do not conflate challenge Satisfied with review Accepted. No agent launcher without explicit prior notice.
